title: [Transform] handle pit index not found error

timeline.body:
Do not fail the transform if pit search fails with index not found as a result of an index that got deleted via ILM, if that index is part of a search that selects indices using a wildcard, e.g. `logs-*`. If pit search fails, the search is retried using search without a pit
context. The 2nd search might fail if the source targets an explicit index. In addition the usage of the pit API can not be disabled by transform.

fixes #81252
relates #81256

Why are we allowing `null` here on the server side? Either it is using `pit` or not.

timeline.body:
This is probably a larger conversation but:
> // do not write default values

Seems like a bad idea as a whole. This means we have to consider older transforms automatically (and unexpectedly) changing their behavior between versions. 

But, I suppose that is a larger idea outside of this PR. To me, being explicit makes more sense.

reply.body: ^ Just a passing thought, I know this won't get adjusted in this PR as we want consistency with how settings are handled.

for pit we are not changing the default. If we decide to change it: yes we need to ensure the behavior works according to the version the transform has been created. Fortunately this is not the case for pit.

But we have changed defaults and e.g. introduced `dates_as_epoch_millis` and `align_checkpoints`. They work by checking the version in addition to the setting, so e.g. for version < 7.11  `dates_as_epoch_millis` is `true`, after 7.11 it is `false`. Note  `dates_as_epoch_millis` does not exist < 7.11

Update has another component: When it rewrites the config it checks the version and e.g. rewrites a 7.11 transform to a current transform, but sets the setting accordingly.

This works actually. We currently have a tiny glitch for `align_checkpoints`, but that fix is in the makings.

Nevertheless this fits to your other comment: settings are returned as Boolean and can be `null`, so the `null` check has to happen on the implementation.

timeline.body: `getUsePit()` should know about the default value and not return a boxed boolean.

reply.body:
yeah, I thought about this, too. The other settings unfortunately do it the same way. I suggest I create a follow up PR and fix it for all.

One of the problems is the version (of the transform config, not the current release version), settings doesn't know the version of the transform and it is not possible to know the version at construction the way parsing works. In addition it seems better to me to keep _settings_ a data container and don't add logic to it.
Having that said, I think a solution for this problem, making this easier to read and more maintainable would be to have a getter with a default:

```
boolean getUsePit(boolean default)
```

The caller can use it like:

```
transformConfig.getSettings().getUsePit(true);
```

In other cases where defaults change:
```
settings.getDatesAsEpochMillis(version.before(Version.V_7_11_0))
```

/CC @przemekwitek WDYT? 

I think with requiring a default, the issue with `align_checkpoints` would not have happened?

`boolean getUsePit(boolean default)`

If we are going to keep them boxed, Java already has a way to handle this with `Optional`. 

So

```
Optional<Boolean> getUsePit()
```
```
getUsePit().orElse(true)
```
For epoch millis
```
getDatesAsEpochMillis().orElse(version.before(Version.V_7_11_0))
```
